subject: Cost parity proposal & replacement feasibility
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@maven-analytics.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@techops.mvn>, legal@maven-analytics.com
Date: 2027-05-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cost parity proposal & replacement feasibility

Hi Aisha,

We kicked off a runway review this week and one of our vendors (EdgeScale) has come back with a pretty aggressive retention offer: cost parity on our monthly spend plus a small pilot credit if we migrate in Q3. Given performance and reliability concerns we've had with them historically, we wanted to check two things with Redwood:

- Can Redwood put together a formal cost-parity proposal that lines up with our token/embedding run-rate?
- What would the expected migration impact be (KV cache migration, model compatibility, downtime windows, ops support)?

If you can share a simple term sheet + any deployment worksheet that maps runtime differences to migration effort, that would help Procurement & Tech Ops make a quick decision.

We need to close vendor decisions by 6/2 to hit procurement cycles, so timing is tight.

Thanks —
Oliver

> We kicked off a runway review this week and one of our vendors (EdgeScale) has come back with a pretty aggressive retention offer...

Hi Oliver — thanks for the context. Looping in Connor (SE) for migration sizing and Ben (sales) for commercial options.

Short answer: we can absolutely present a competitive package, but the exact structure depends on 1) committed runtime (prepay vs. monthly), 2) token/embedding mix, and 3) whether you need Guaranteed Capacity during peak windows.

What I can do now:
- Share a compact deployment worksheet (attached) that maps your current peak/avg token profiles to expected throughput & recommended quantization.
- Draft a short term-sheet with a conditional migration credit and accelerated onboarding support.

Next steps: if you can send last 3 months of token/hour distribution (or approve the attached worksheet with our estimations), Connor and I will produce a line-item price match + migration plan by EOD 5/26.

Best,
Aisha Rahman

Hi Oliver — quick technical note from the SE side.

Summary of migration considerations:
- KV cache: we recommend a short live sync window (48–72 hrs) with prefix warming; full cold-start fallback possible but would add 6–12 hours to SLA for the heaviest endpoints.
- Model variants: if you move from an fp16 runtime to a quantized runtime there may be a small P95 latency increase (~5–12%) but token cost falls ~30–40% depending on quantization.
- Data egress: if you currently have models hosted in-region and move to a different region, egress charges could be material — we map that in the worksheet.
- Ops support: we can provide an augmented SRE pairing for the first 4 weeks (1x SRE + 1x SE) as part of a migration credit bundle.

I've populated the attached maven-deployment-worksheet.xlsx with conservative numbers based on your public post-run metrics; feel free to flag anything that looks off.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@maven-analytics.com>

Date: 2027-05-25T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cost parity proposal & replacement feasibility

Thanks Aisha / Connor — this is helpful. Two follow-ups:

1) Can you commit to a written price match that aligns with the numbers in the worksheet? We need explicit per-token and per-embedding unit pricing for the first 12 months (we're treating year one as the proof-of-performance period).
2) Procurement is asking for a migration credit figure (flat credit or invoice-level credit) and a clear list of what's included in onboarding (SRE hours, runbook, rollback plan).

If you can put those in a one-page term sheet, we can route to Procurement + Legal quickly. Also — any timing constraints on when an offer expires?

Oliver
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@maven-analytics.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-26T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cost parity proposal & replacement feasibility

Hi Oliver — appreciate the fast cadence. Attaching a short term sheet (redwood-competitive-match-term-sheet.pdf) with our commercial offer. Key points:

- Pricing: match EdgeScale effective unit price for Year 1 subject to a 12-month minimum committed consumption (we used your worksheet to estimate the minimum).
- Migration credit: $50,000 one-time credit applied at invoice after go-live (covers SRE pairing and onboarding runbooks).
- Pilot support: 4-week SRE/SE pairing included; rollback/runbook and a 2-week performance guarantee window.
- Legal/contract: MSA + SOW; we can accommodate your standard amendments but the above commercial items are tied to the 12-month commit.
- Offer expiry: 5 business days from this email (deadline 5/31 COB).

Numbers (high level):
- Token generation: $0.0007 / token (year 1 matched price)
- Embedding units: $0.0009 / unit
- Estimated 12-month committed spend: $1.45M (per worksheet)

If that looks acceptable I'll have Legal push a draft MSA + SOW and we can route DocuSign. Also pinged our Finance manager to prepare updated PO routing notes.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Manager, Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Ben / Aisha — thanks, that structure is workable. We accept the commercial outline in principle: year-1 match + $50k migration credit conditioned on 12-mo commit.

Procurement will circulate a purchase order once Legal and your counsel confirm the MSA redlines. Please have your legal counterpart reach out to legal@maven-analytics.com and share the draft MSA + SOW and the term sheet PDF you referenced.

We'll also confirm final token counts from the worksheet, but plan to route this to exec sign-off later this week.
